verses.text: King Solomon loved many foreign women besides Pharaoh's daughter. They were Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women.

The LORD had told the Israelites about these nations, “You must not join yourselves to them, and they must not join themselves to you. They'll surely turn your hearts toward their gods.” But Solomon held on to these women in love.
He had seven hundred wives of royal rank and three hundred concubines. His wives turned his heart away.
When Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart toward other gods. His heart wasn't wholly devoted to the LORD his God as his father's heart had been.
Solomon followed Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Milcom, the detestable god of the Ammonites.
Solomon did what was evil in the LORD's sight. He didn't follow the LORD wholeheartedly as his father David had.
On the mountain facing Jerusalem, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable god of Moab, and for Molech, the detestable god of the Ammonites.
He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.
The LORD was angry with Solomon because his heart had turned from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
He had commanded Solomon to keep away from other gods, but Solomon disobeyed the LORD's command.
So the LORD told Solomon, “Because you've done this and broken my covenant and the statutes I commanded you to keep, I'll tear the kingdom away from you and give it to one of your servants.
For the sake of your father David, I won't do this during your lifetime. I'll tear it out of your son's hands.
Even then, I won't take the whole kingdom. I'll leave one tribe to your son for the sake of my servant David and Jerusalem, the city I've chosen.”
The LORD raised up an opponent against Solomon named Hadad the Edomite, a descendant of Edom's king.
Back when David was in Edom, Joab the army commander went up to bury the dead and struck down every male in Edom.
Joab and all Israel stayed there for six months, until every male in Edom had been cut down.
Hadad was only a small child at the time. He escaped to Egypt with some Edomites who had served his father.
They left Midian, went to Paran, and took some men from there with them into Egypt. Pharaoh king of Egypt gave Hadad a house, a supply of food, and land.
Pharaoh took such a liking to Hadad that he gave him his own wife's sister in marriage, the sister of Queen Tahpenes.
Tahpenes' sister bore Hadad a son named Genubath. Tahpenes weaned him in Pharaoh's palace, and he lived there among Pharaoh's sons.
When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had died and Joab the army commander was dead too, he told Pharaoh, “Let me leave so I can go home to my own country.”
Pharaoh asked, “What have you lacked here with me that makes you want to go back to your country?” Hadad answered, “Nothing. Please just let me go.”
God raised up another opponent, Rezon son of Eliada. He had fled from his master Hadadezer, king of Zobah.
When David killed the men of Zobah, Rezon gathered a band of men and became their leader. They went to Damascus, settled there, and took power in the city.
Alongside the trouble Hadad caused, Rezon opposed Israel throughout Solomon's reign. He despised Israel and ruled over Syria.
Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah and one of Solomon's servants, also rebelled against the king. His mother Zeruah was a widow.
Here's how he came to rebel. Solomon was building the Millo and repairing the breach in the defenses of his father David's City.
Jeroboam was a capable man. When Solomon saw how hard the young man worked, he put him in charge of all the labor from the house of Joseph.
One day Jeroboam left Jerusalem, and Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh met him on the road. Ahijah was wearing a new garment, and the two men were alone in the open country.
Ahijah took off the new garment he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
He told Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces. This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I'm going to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hands and give ten tribes to you.
He'll keep one tribe for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I've chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.

This is because they've abandoned me and worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They haven't followed my ways, done what's right in my eyes, or kept my statutes and rulings as Solomon's father David did.
“‘I won't take the whole kingdom out of Solomon's hands. I'll let him rule for the rest of his life for the sake of my chosen servant David, who kept my commands and statutes.
I'll take the kingdom from Solomon's son and give ten tribes to you.
I'll give one tribe to his son, so my servant David will always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city I've chosen for my name.
I'll take you and make you king over Israel. You'll rule over all your heart desires.

If you listen to everything I command, follow my ways, do what's right in my eyes, and keep my statutes and commands as my servant David did, I'll be with you. I'll establish a lasting royal family for you as I did for David, and I'll give you Israel.
I'll bring trouble on David's descendants because of this, but it won't last forever.’”
Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam escaped to Shishak king of Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died.
The rest of Solomon's acts, everything he did, and his wisdom are recorded in the Book of the Acts of Solomon.
Solomon ruled over all Israel from Jerusalem for forty years.
Solomon died and joined his ancestors. He was buried in his father David's City, and his son Rehoboam became king in his place.
